title: Incorrect pairs counted by summing mismatches
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $p$ be a deterministic one-way protocol that takes an $n$-bit Boolean string from Alice and an index in $[n]$ from Bob, and outputs a Boolean. The number of input pairs $(x,i)$ on which $p$ disagrees with the Index function equals the sum, over all $n$-bit strings $x$, of the number of indices $i$ on which $p$ disagrees with the $i$th bit of $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic one-way protocol with finite nonempty message set, Alice's input an $n$-bit Boolean string, Bob's input an index in $[n]$, and Boolean output
replaced:
The number of incorrect input pairs $(x, i)$ of $p$ equals the sum, over all strings
$x \in \{0,1\}^n$, of the number of indices $i$ on which $p$ errs at $x$:
\[
  \abs{\mathrm{badPairs}(p)} = \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} \abs{\mathrm{mismatch}(p, x)}.
\]
